messages.subject: survival in MARK - incomplete capture history
messages.subject_clean: survival in MARK - incomplete capture history
messages.body_plain:
Hi all!

I am producing survival estimates from Constant Effort Sites data using MARK.
I used dot for the missing visits in capture history:

1892 0000001000.    1
1893 ....001....    1
1894 ....001....    1
1895 ....001....    1
1896 ....001....    1
1897 ....001....    1
1898 ....001....    1
1899 .....100000    1
1900 .....100000    1

However, now I found that programs for GOF tests - RELEASE and U-CARE - are
not working with this data at all. I've been told by Olivier that this is
kind of non-standard and he seemed surprised that MARK allows this. But how else
would you specify a missing visit (NA)? Seems quite a common situation in
real life data.

So I have two questions:

1) How can I specify missing visits to MARK? Does it work with the dot? I
was using it like this and supposed it works but now when I look in the MARK
book (http://www.phidot.org/software/mark/docs/book/), the only
documentation available, it is not mentioned there!

2) Are there any ways how to run GOF tests on data with missing visits?

Thanks a lot,

	Tomas

PS: I am using newest versions of RMark R package for RELEASE and R2ucare for U-CARE in R.

messages.subject_clean: survival in MARK - incomplete capture history
messages.body_plain:
Dear Tomas,

I believe that you can discard the capture histories like the one in the 2nd row. I think they are like a caphist with a one in the very last occasion; they don't contain any extractable info about survival via de CJS model.

Otherwise, why don't you aggregate the data to the m-array and then run a Bayesian posterior predictive check ? That's perhaps not as good as the diagnostic checks in RELEASE (because it doesn't tell you in which way the data are problematic), but at least it's somehting.

best regards  ---- Marc

messages.body_plain:
Hello all,
We are building a dynamic occupancy model for data from a long-term bird survey. Multiple species are recorded during the survey but we are interested in only 1, Species A. In addition to static or dynamic abiotic covariates on detection and occupancy of Species A we would like to add the presence of Species B as a covariate on occupancy. Can anyone point us to a discussion or manuscript that might give some example model formulation on how to do this? We will need to model occupancy of Species B in parallel with Species A and then add that occupancy as 0/1 to the covariates on Species A occupancy but not exactly sure how to do that. Thanks for any insight.

messages.subject: RE: Occupancy dependence among species
messages.body_plain:
Hi Tony,

Do you have access to ‘the Kery books’? I think there is an example in the Bayesian Pop Analysis book where the occupancy of a bird is modeled using estimated jointly with the occupancy of red squirrels – and then one (sqwurl), is used as a covariate on the other (bird). This is done using a Bayesian analysis due to the convenience of being able to estimate the latent z’s in the mcmc and use them in the linear predictor. So, for your uni-directional example (A influenced by B, but B not influenced by A), and where you aren’t necessarily interested in inferring co-occurrence, then I think this approach does what you need.

Let me know if you don’t have the book and I can fax you the relevant pages. It might also be the case that this is an example in one of the workshops I have attended, so, if it’s not in the book let me know and I will dig out that material too.

Good luck!

Chris

We are building a dynamic occupancy model for data from a long-term bird survey. Multiple species are recorded during the survey but we are interested in only 1, Species A. In addition to static or dynamic abiotic covariates on detection and occupancy of Species A we would like to add the presence of Species B as a covariate on occupancy. Can anyone point us to a discussion or manuscript that might give some example model formulation on how to do this? We will need to model occupancy of Species B in parallel with Species A and then add that occupancy as 0/1 to the covariates on Species A occupancy but not exactly sure how to do that. Thanks for any insight.

messages.body_plain:
Dear Antonela,

this is due to missing values in the covariates. Cases with missing covariates are discarded, so when you fit, for instance, the constant model and one with a covariate that has at least one NA, then the two models are fit to two different (sub)sets of the full umf data frame. You have to restrict your data set feeded into the umf to the complete cases. This has been discussed on the list before, please check the archives.

Best regards  --- Marc

messages.body_plain:
Hi Jenny,

Just stream of consciousness here (caveat emptor): am I off-base, or are these two models suggesting completely different effects of betaHab[1]? Is it possible there's some sort of confoundment between covariates for theta and psi (or alternatively, are the categories being used for theta all-inclusive...e.g., only three parameters are identifiable)? Other alternatives might include poor tuning of the jump parameters (see Mike Meredith's post below regarding adaptation vs. burn-in) and/or just getting stuck in a strange part of the parameter space [the prior for int.psi/theta makes me a little uneasy. You certainly seem to have enough data to escape any prior; but you're putting tremendous prior weight on intercept values that are less than .01 or greater than .99 on the probability scale...maybe the standard int.theta~U(0,1), beta0.beta<-inv.logit(int.theta) back-transform would work well here]?  I feel as through trace-plots might give you a sense of whether this is a data issue or an algorithmic/prior issue...are the samples of specific parameters completely correlated, or taking a long time to move towards a stationary distribution, or getting stuck frequently, or some combination there-of (etc.)?

John
